about: Pinyin to IPA for AISHELL-3, with the source of each choice. Read on Nov 10, 2026, Pacific time. Used by AISHELL3.py. This is a phonemic table. It gives one fixed IPA string for each initial and final, so it shows no allophones, no coarticulation and no speaker accent beyond what the pinyin writes.

sources.UW: Handel and Tahmoresi, University of Washington, Chinese 342, IPA pages: finals https://courses.washington.edu/chin342/ipa/finals.html and consonants https://courses.washington.edu/chin342/ipa/consonants.html. Read on Nov 10, 2026 through a text extraction of the pages. The site says its transcription is broad and writes the glides as i, u and y. The consonant table came out flattened, so a few pairings follow the cell order and are not checked on the rendered page
sources.WB: Wikibooks, Chinese (Mandarin), Pronunciation of Finals, section on the final i, https://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Chinese/Pronunciation_of_Finals. Read on Nov 10, 2026 in a search extract. It lists the buzzed vowel of i after z c s zh ch sh r as [ɻ̩], [ɹ̩] without saying which goes where
sources.WIKI: Wikipedia, Standard Chinese phonology and Help:IPA/Mandarin, for the Chao tone letters of the four full tones, read on Nov 10, 2026 in a search extract
sources.LIBRE: LibreTexts, CHN 101 Beginning Mandarin, 1.2.1 Mandarin Phonology (Sound System) II, section Neutral Tone, https://human.libretexts.org/Workbench/CHN_101%3A_Beginning_Mandarin/01%3A_Introduction/1.02%3A_Pre-Unit_2/1.2.01%3A_Mandarin_Phonology_(Sound_System)_II, read on Nov 10, 2026 in a search extract. It gives the pitch of a neutral tone as 2 after tone 1, 3 after tone 2, 4 after tone 3 and 1 after tone 4
sources.PINYIN: Hanyu Pinyin spelling rules for y, w, u after j q x, and the written forms ui, un and iu, as listed on the Wikipedia pinyin table https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinyin_table, read on Nov 10, 2026 in a search extract. AISHELL-3 writes the letter ü as v (ReadMe.txt and content.txt)

r.note: UW lists r as ɹ. Other sources write ɻ or ʐ. Flagged for Alex

finals_notes.o: UW gives o and uo one final, uɔ. Pinyin writes o for uo after b p m f (PINYIN), and o alone is the syllable o
finals_notes.iou uei uen: the base forms of iu, ui and un, which pinyin writes short after an initial (PINYIN). The no-initial spellings you and wei and wen reach them
finals_notes.ueng: weng. It is not in the UW table, which has no row for it. Built as uen with ŋ (derived, not in the source)
finals_notes.iong: UW writes it yuŋ. The units are y u ŋ

retroflex.note: WB lists the pair [ɻ̩], [ɹ̩] for the letter i after these initials. Which symbol goes after the dental and which after the retroflex initials is the usual reading and is not stated in the extract. Not verified

tones.note: Chao letters for the four tones, from WIKI. The neutral tone 5 takes its pitch from the last full tone before it, 2 after tone 1, 3 after tone 2, 4 after tone 3 and 1 after tone 4, from LIBRE. So a run of neutral tones keeps the pitch of the full tone before the run. LIBRE does not say what a run does, or what a neutral tone at the start of an utterance does, and both of those choices are the loader's own, with ˧ at the start. Not verified

skip_syllables.jv: a nonstandard spelling, since pinyin writes ü after j as u, once in the archive
skip_syllables.din: not a pinyin syllable, once in the archive
skip_syllables.lo: a particle, 3 times in the archive. The table reads the final o as uɔ, which holds after b, p, m and f only, not for this particle, so lo is skipped and counted
